body: sprint-work-item-operates-the-product: Evidence, re-verified: the Work items template at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:37-40 still reads only 'The implementation units that realize the deltas ... describes the outcome, not the method.' No text in plan-sprint SKILL.md, core.md, or sprint-document.md says a work item changes the product. The only nearby rule is execution step 11 at sprint-document.md:170 ('Work unsupervised to a defensible done. Do not pause for approval, confirmation, or progress checks.'). Sign-off (plan-sprint/SKILL.md:148-150) runs the compliance reviewer on the corpus deltas alone. The notes review (core.md:324-377) looks only for behavior changes and compatibility breaks. /converge's owner list (converge/SKILL.md:123) files 'every other item that needs the owner's judgment' and refuses no operator act. Rot: the record was filed from a consumer project at v25.3.0. It names the materialized .claude/skills/plan-sprint/ files as suite-owned and carries an upstream draft. In this repo the canonical source is project-owned under plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ (review/project.md, 'The root and what is out of scope'). So the change is the project's own product: drop the upstream draft and keep the category off upstream. The owner's ruling quoted in the problem was given in that consumer project; this record carries no ruling. Mechanism: no step of planning tests what kind of outcome a work item names. Execution then files a build task that operates a stack, and certification judges the tree, the checks, and a drive on its own fresh stack, so it cannot see the result and files an owner task instead. Corpus: concept:sprint says 'the flat, unordered work items that realize them' and is silent on a work item that uses the product. concept:issue Boundaries says 'the intake is a holding area, not a work tracker, and nothing is worked to completion in it', which bears on option C. story:plan-a-sprint promises a sprint 'any executor can realize ... without re-deriving it'. story:certify-completion promises to 'know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered'. concept:completion-contract scopes done to 'the change'. No artifact says a work item must change the product, so the rule adds a promise; the owner must choose. Harm: no accept-list entry applies; this is a judgment issue. Options: A, as filed: state the rule in the Draft phase and the template, check every work item at sign-off, and state in the execution boilerplate that nothing needs an owner action. Cost: sign-off gains a work-item scope it does not have today. B, statements only. Cost: no check fails on violation, against the cheatsheet's Mechanical Checks rule ('Every written constraint needs a check that fails on violation'). C, A plus refusal in /converge's owner list and /triage-issues (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:123, skills/triage-issues/). Cost: a real certification gap phrased as an owner act could be retired unread. Missed D: let the code planner kick back an operator-act item under its existing step 8 (core.md:274, 'Kick the work item back where it cannot be built as drafted'). Cost: lowest; it reuses an existing check, but it catches the item only after drafting. Missed E: any of A to D pairs with a concept:sprint delta that states the rule in Boundaries, since the promise belongs in the corpus. Siblings: sprint-certification-drives-only-sprint-stories, agents-route-clear-defects-to-the-owner.

new-issues-show-no-unread-mark: Evidence, re-verified; the filed mechanism holds. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:473-474 (unread) counts only agent messages whose read is null. defaults() at :611-613 gives a new record 'messages': []. revise at :707-708 records a first routing (an issue neither routed nor ruled) with reason 'first routing' and no message. The page's isUnread at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/browser/src/lib/api.js:79 is 'summary.unread > 0'. IssueList.svelte:71-73 shows the 'N new' tag only where isUnread holds. No field records whether the owner has ever opened an issue; 'issues read <id>' marks agent messages read and nothing else. Also, api.js:87 leaves state 'verified' out of the 'unread' filter, so a defect issue never lists as unread even when it holds unread messages. Mechanism: an issue's first analysis lives in its problem, options, and recommendation fields, never in a message, so a new issue's unread count is 0 until an agent writes a message. Corpus: decision:agent-revisions-reach-the-owner says 'A first routing stays silent', with the rationale 'A first routing already shows the issue as needing a ruling'. That rationale covers routing, not filing, and does not hold for a verified defect issue, which never needs a ruling. story:see-new-analysis asks for 'a way to see which issues, open or closed, have new answers or revisions since I last read them, whoever wrote them'. It does not say whether an issue the owner has never read counts. decision:closed-answers-count-as-new covers answers on closed issues only. Settling whether filing counts as new analysis widens a promise, so the owner chooses. Harm: no accept-list entry applies; this is a judgment issue. Options: A, record the owner's first open of an issue (set by 'issues read' and the dashboard's POST /api/issue/<id>/read) and mark an unopened issue new. Cost: a new record field, and a migration so existing issues do not all show as new; amend decision:agent-revisions-reach-the-owner, or add a decision, to say filing counts. B, have 'issues file' write an unread agent 'filed' message for every issue an agent files (never for one the owner files), so the existing unread count carries it. Cost: no schema change, but one message per issue that says nothing new. C, keep the behavior and amend the decision's rationale to say needs-ruling is the signal for judgment issues and /plan-sprint's Frame list is the signal for defect issues. Cost: the owner's harm stands. D, a per-browser 'since your last visit' mark comparing each issue's opened time to the viewer's last visit. Cost: no store change, but it lives in one browser only and misses issues the owner saw elsewhere. Settle the api.js:87 filter with whichever option is picked. body: sprint-certification-drives-only-sprint-stories: Evidence, re-verified: decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user Choice reads "`/converge` in drive mode gives every story its own driver once per run, and sprint certification does the same for the stories a sprint adds or amends." plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:102 (sprint step 4, the drive) runs drive mode "over those stories alone", the stories the sprint's deltas add or amend and those its work items name. skills/converge/prompts/merge.md:40-50 ("The drive's failures") sends a failure whose code stood the same at the base to `backlog`; the owner keeps that scope test. No suite text sets when a drive run must happen: drive mode runs on the owner's cadence. The filed problem has not rotted. Mechanism: a story no sprint amends is never driven until a drive run, so a legacy failure surfaces only in a later certification that happens to amend the story, and the scope test then moves it to the intake while the sprint closes. Corpus: drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user fixes the certification's drive scope in its Choice; story:certify-completion promises "so that 'done' means the same thing for every sprint" and is silent on stories the sprint does not touch. Every option below edits the decision's Choice, so the route is question. Harm: a sprint closes with a story the owner believes works still failing; no accept-list entry decides this, it is what the product commits to. Options: A. certification drives every story: every closed sprint leaves every story driven; cost: every certification pays drive mode's full cost, which the decision's rationale names "where a run spends its tokens". B. drive the sprint's stories plus every story whose citing code the change touched, found by @story annotations in the changed files: cost scales with the change; misses a story whose code carries no annotation, and a story broken by a change to code it calls but does not cite. C. /plan-sprint refuses to start until a drive run has passed since the last close, filing its failures as defect issues the sprint can pull in: failures meet the owner at Frame, not as a surprise; cost: a full drive run per sprint, before planning, and a gate on /plan-sprint the decision and the plan-sprint skill must name. D (filer missed): /plan-sprint reports at Frame how many sprints have closed since the last drive run and offers a drive run first, without refusing: no new gate; cost: the owner's cadence stays the only guard. Rule with drive-pass-is-one-try and merge-sorts-drive-failures-off-the-story.

drive-pass-is-one-try: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/drive.md:23 has the driver try each surface the story is offered through and judge each on its own; drive.md:41-43 reads "For each surface you try, stop at the first of these: achieved: you got the benefit the 'so that' clause names". So one path per surface, and the driver stops at the first path that works. drive.md:48 adds only promised refusals ("where the story promises one, try it"). The filed problem has not rotted. Mechanism: `achieved` ends the surface's drive, so paths the driver did not choose (a flag, a control pressed first, an order of actions, a second session) go untried, and certification reads the pass as the story working. Corpus: decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user says the driver "works out from the running product how to get the benefit on every surface the story is offered through" and "Nothing about a drive is written down between runs"; it asks for every surface, never every path within one. story:certify-completion: "so that 'done' means the same thing for every sprint". Widening a drive from one path to every path widens what the decision commits a drive to, so the route is question. Harm: a pass reports a story works while another path fails (the reporter's two cases: the mark stepper's first Next, and a device listing's --since/--until against its help); a judgment issue, no accept-list entry decides it. Options: A. the driver lists every path per surface (each verb and flag, each page control, each order), drives each, reports the list; the merge refiles an undriven path: most coverage; cost grows with the product's flags and controls, and the merge must judge the list's completeness. B. two independent drivers per story, pass only where both pass: cost doubles every drive; two drivers may still take the same path. C. keep one try: cost as filed, a pass can miss a failing path. D (filer missed): the driver drives every variant the story's own text names (find-records' "narrowed by time and by the values of their fields" gives each narrowing a drive) plus the order a first-time user would act in: bounded by the story's text; misses a path the text does not name. Rule with sprint-certification-drives-only-sprint-stories and merge-sorts-drive-failures-off-the-story.

merge-sorts-drive-failures-off-the-story: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/merge.md:44 (defect bullet of "The drive's failures") still reads "A stuck story with no such message (the user needed a page, a verb, or a flow the product does not offer) is not a defect for this run: sort it `not-owed` and record a question naming what the user was missing." merge.md:50 still reads "Where the corpus does not decide whether the product owes what the driver tried to get, sort it `not-owed`". merge.md:44 also says a story defect merges "as a defect (entry A3 unless another entry fits better)", but merge.md:20 (step 2 for reports) has the agent apply the accept list to the harm, and nothing says which test governs a drive failure. The filed problem has not rotted. Mechanism: path 1, the stuck rule sorts by the failure's kind (stuck, no message), not by whether the story's benefit names the missing flow, so it contradicts the defect bullet's own test; path 2, nothing tells the merge that a sprint work item is not the story or a decision it cites; path 3, nothing tells the merge that the accept list already covers a story failure. Corpus: decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user: "A merge agent sorts each failure as a defect the story or a decision owes, as something the corpus does not promise, or as a failure of the environment." That rule decides path 1 and path 2: where the story's text names the flow or the true report the driver did not get, the failure is a defect the story owes, whatever the failure's kind or a work item's wording. decision:accept-list-decides-defects: "a driver reports each failure it meets, and the merge sorts those failures against the list"; A3 names "every failure the drive records" among its sites and A8 counts "a commitment of a live artifact under .ok-planner/design/". So option A's clause "the accept list does not clear a drive failure" contradicts accept-list-decides-defects as worded; the compliant wording is that a failure of what the story's text names is covered by A3 and A8, and no "leaves standing" line clears it because an entry holds. The tooling the change edits: skills/converge/prompts/merge.md, "The drive's failures". A stated rule (the two decisions above) decides that change, so the author may write a generated ruling: merge.md's drive section sorts a failure as a defect wherever the story's text names what the driver could not get (a missing flow included, and a page or message that tells the user something false), sorts not-owed only where the driver sought something beyond the story's text and its decisions, and names A3 and A8 as the entries that cover a story failure. Path 2 also meets the sprint catalog: where a sprint work item's wording contradicts a story, that is C4 (a commitment contradicted) in sprint mode, not a reason to sort not-owed. Harm: a sprint closes with a story failing and no defect listed. Options: A as filed, with the accept-list clause reworded as above; B. A plus a quote from the story required on every stuck or not-owed sort, refiled without one: cost, one more refile round per bad sort; C. keep the prompt and rule each not-owed question at /plan-sprint: cost, the owner's attention on each, and sprints close with failing stories meanwhile. Rule with agents-route-clear-defects-to-the-owner, drive-pass-is-one-try, and sprint-certification-drives-only-sprint-stories.

agents-route-clear-defects-to-the-owner: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:45-62 (OWNER_PATHS) still classes every path under `.ok-planner/design/` as `corpus`, `_discover/` included, and admin/converge:caller_kind (around line 1691) still skips only `record` and `suite` files, so a consumer's `_discover/` note is still repointed. In this repository the notes now sit at .ok-planner/history/discover/ (commit 515ac2d), so this tree no longer shows the instance. The instance itself is ruled: converge-repoints-observation-notes-and-migration-docs carries the owner's ruling "Fix it. The notes under .ok-planner/design/_discover/ are records ... This is a clear defect, not a question." That ruling awaits a sprint; this issue asks about the prompts' habit, which still stands. Prompts as they stand: skills/triage-issues/prompts/triage.md:37 already reads "No: the corpus or a stated rule decides the end state, and only the mechanism is open. Route `defect`", and its doubt test asks whether a fixer would have to edit a file under .ok-planner/design/; both date from v23.0.0, before this issue, and triage still routed the case question. skills/converge/prompts/merge.md:33 (ownership test) sends a report to `judgment` when `review owner` prints `corpus` for a file of the fix, and no line tells the merge that where a code list contradicts a rule the corpus states, the code list is the site (A8) and the fix lies in project code. Mechanism: agents take OWNER_PATHS' classing as the rule, so a fix named at the note reads as a corpus change; and concept:design-corpus counts "a point-in-time discovery scaffold" inside the corpus and never says whether it is a record, which let triage read the record list as a corpus commitment. Corpus: decision:runs-fix-what-the-project-owns: agents "fix a clear defect in every file the project owns", a record "keeps what it said when it was written", and filing a clear defect "spends the owner's attention on a fix the rules already decide"; decision:whole-file-ownership: converge rewrites a line in a tracked file "other than a record"; accept list A8. The tooling the change edits: skills/converge/prompts/merge.md (report judging and the ownership test), skills/triage-issues/prompts/triage.md, skills/triage-issues/prompts/author.md. Harm: clear defects reach the owner as questions; no accept-list entry, a tooling judgment. Options: A. teach merge, triage, and author that code departing from a one-form corpus rule is an A8 defect even where the departure predates the change, and route it defect; cost: agents must judge whether the corpus rule leaves one form, and an ambiguous corpus (as concept:design-corpus is on records) still needs the owner. B. leave the prompts: cost, the owner rules each case. C (filer missed): one line in merge.md's ownership test only: where a report's file is `corpus` because a code list classes it so and a corpus rule decides the class, the site is the code list and the fix lies in project code; narrower than A, leaves triage as it stands since triage.md:37 already says it. Rule with converge-repoints-observation-notes-and-migration-docs, discover-design-offers-to-archive-its-notes, and merge-sorts-drive-failures-off-the-story.

discover-design-offers-to-archive-its-notes: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md:28 places the notes at `_discover/` ("phase 1 scaffolding"), :35 calls them "the trail of what was observed", :46 aborts on non-empty catalogs and says "keeping `_discover/` makes phase 1 incremental", :62 (final report) and :738 (re-run) offer no archive step. skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:339: "`_discover/` scaffolding is point-in-time and exempt." skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md:228: "Flag nothing under `_discover/`." scripts/review:45-62 (OWNER_PATHS) classes the folder as corpus. In this repository .ok-planner/design/_discover/ no longer exists; the owner moved the notes to .ok-planner/history/discover/ (commit 515ac2d). The filed problem has not rotted. Mechanism: once phase 2 fills the catalogs the skill refuses to run again, so nothing reads the notes as input, yet they stay where converge and review read live corpus text. Corpus: concept:design-corpus, What it is: the corpus is the three catalogs "plus a point-in-time discovery scaffold that feeds the initial extraction", and Boundaries: "The discovery scaffold is point-in-time and exempt from the durable rules." Moving the scaffold to history/ after extraction narrows what the concept says the corpus holds, so options A and B need a delta to that concept; decision:whole-file-ownership: "a migration moves them [records] and never rewrites their bodies", which a move keeps. No story covers /discover-design's end state. Harm: converge reads the notes as live text and rewrites them (made script-materialization.md false in this repo); the owner's ruling on converge-repoints-observation-notes-and-migration-docs already fixes that harm for notes left in place. Options: A. offer once at the end of a run that filled the catalogs, move on yes, and name the archived folder as the restore source in the re-run section: cost, one question per bootstrap and a concept delta. B. always move, no question: cost, no consent, a concept delta, and an incremental re-run must restore the notes by hand. C. leave the notes and rely on converge's fix: cost, notes stay among corpus readers (surface-corpus, catalog readers) forever. D (filer missed): /ok's converge core offers the move as a cleanup offer whenever the catalogs are non-empty and `_discover/` exists: reaches projects bootstrapped before the change; cost, the administration gains a judgment the skill could ask once. Rule with converge-repoints-observation-notes-and-migration-docs and agents-route-clear-defects-to-the-owner.
